title: CRRT circuit complication
banner: DRAFT, NOT clinically reviewed. Fictional scenario specification; never imported, published or shown to learners.
learning_objectives: Check the patient first when a circuit alarm sounds.
Use the device's own instructions and avoid disabling alarms.
Know when to return blood, stop treatment, document and notify the prescriber.
Report under-delivery of the prescribed dose.

sources.use: Targeted 2026 consensus statement 10 on possible citrate accumulation; not a randomized trial or full guideline review.
2026 multidisciplinary ICU RRT guideline: anticoagulation recommendations 4.4–4.6 and dose-in-CRRT discussion; selected HTML sections, not full appraisal

required_sources: Manufacturer operator's manual for the unit's machine and software version
gaps: No published clinical scenario may exist until the review phase: this is a specification only.
The branching content, consequences and scoring are the author's reading of the cited sources and have had no clinical review.
The pathway is specific to one machine family and says actions follow local practice guidelines.

Selected January 2026 RRT guideline and May 2026 citrate Delphi monitoring statements are mapped. Exact schedules, thresholds, citrate/calcium adjustments, drug dosing and weaning remain specialist and local decisions. KDIGO 2026 remains a public-review draft, not a final replacement.

Scenario has been limited to patient-first assessment, competent CRRT-operator escalation, interruption documentation, and approved procedure boundaries; it does not teach independent troubleshooting or blood return.
permissions: Cited sources are paraphrased only; see the licensing register for each source's reproduction status.
AHS pathway: licence not stated; verify.
setting: A fictional adult on continuous renal replacement therapy on a fictional unit.

steps.info: Immediately after repositioning an adult on CRRT, an access-pressure alarm recurs and the blood pump stops. The patient has been coughing. The cause of the alarm and circuit safety have not yet been established.
steps.prompt: What should happen before any attempt to restart the circuit?

options.text: Assess the patient and circuit display, request a trained CRRT operator, and report the alarm and recent bed movement. Only a competent operator should check access/return tubing and catheter issues under this device's approved local alarm procedure; do not reflexively clear alarms.
options.feedback: The Alberta Health Services 2025 alarm pathway is specific to its CRRT machine and clinical setting. Patient assessment and prompt operator escalation come first; catheter manipulation, line checks and alarm clearance are not generic instructions for an untrained learner.
options.consequence: Patient assessment and trained device review may identify an access or circuit problem without bypassing safety features.

options.text: Press override and restart because the alarm is probably a false alarm.
options.feedback: Alarm off, disable and override buttons decrease alarm sensitivity and are not a fix.
options.consequence: An override could conceal an unresolved access or circuit problem.

options.text: Turn the blood flow to the maximum the machine allows.
options.feedback: Do not independently increase blood flow to suppress an alarm. Check the patient and escalate to the trained operator who follows the device-specific procedure.
options.consequence: Increasing blood flow without assessment could worsen access problems and delay safe treatment.

steps.info: At the next shared checkpoint, access and return alarms recur despite trained checks. There is no obvious catheter fault and delivered treatment time is falling. Circuit safety and whether blood can safely be returned remain uncertain.
steps.prompt: How should the nurse respond to persistent interruption without assuming that blood return is safe?

options.text: Escalate persistent alarms and interruption to the responsible CRRT-trained team and prescriber. Do not attempt blood return unless the trained operator confirms it is safe under the current device instructions and local procedure. Document lost treatment and any blood loss.
options.feedback: The AHS pathway is specific to its machine and clinical setting. Blood return is not automatic: if clotting or another circuit safety hazard is suspected, do not attempt return before an authorised trained operator establishes the safe pathway. Do not override safety alarms.
options.consequence: The trained operator determines whether blood return is safe; timely escalation may limit avoidable downtime or blood loss and support a revised treatment plan.

options.text: Keep restarting the treatment until it runs and tell the doctor at the end of the shift.
options.feedback: Repeated restarts waste treatment time and delay escalation.
options.consequence: Repeated restarting could delay specialist review while prescribed therapy is missed.

options.text: Clamp the lines and leave the circuit until the next shift.
options.feedback: Leaving a stopped circuit without trained assessment and escalation is unsafe. Blood return may itself be contraindicated; the trained team determines safe termination and records any blood loss.
options.consequence: Leaving a stopped circuit could permit clotting or other complications without appropriate assessment.

steps.info: At the final shared checkpoint, treatment is stopped and the physician is informed. Delivered therapy is below prescription. Regional citrate was used; systemic ionized calcium is falling and the total-to-ionized calcium ratio is rising. The cause of these changes requires urgent specialist assessment.
steps.prompt: Which treatment-delivery and biochemical trends should be communicated before the prescription is reviewed?

observations.label: Anticoagulation
observations.value: Regional citrate used during interrupted treatment

options.text: Document alarms, downtime, delivered treatment and net fluid balance. If regional citrate anticoagulation is in use, report falling systemic ionized calcium, a rising total-to-ionized calcium ratio, increasing calcium requirements or worsening acid-base findings, and coordinate the prescribed response.
options.feedback: KDIGO supports assessment of delivered treatment. The 2026 Delphi consensus identifies falling systemic ionized calcium, increasing calcium needs, a raised total-to-ionized calcium ratio and metabolic acidosis as findings that may suggest citrate accumulation in context. No single finding establishes the diagnosis. Escalate the trend and follow the prescribed specialist response; do not independently adjust citrate, calcium or fluid removal. The January 2026 multidisciplinary RRT guideline distinguishes prescribed from delivered clearance because interruptions reduce effective therapy. Net fluid removal and solute-clearance dose are separate prescription components; do not increase fluid removal simply to compensate for downtime. The guideline also calls for reassessment of anticoagulation if citrate accumulation occurs; the May 2026 Delphi consensus discusses individualized specialist adjustments and alternatives when abnormalities persist. These are not instructions to alter device settings independently.
options.consequence: Reporting downtime, net balance and biochemical trends may help the team identify inadequate delivery and possible citrate accumulation in context.

options.text: Record only that the machine alarmed.
options.feedback: Recording only the alarm omits the treatment interruption, delivered therapy and fluid balance, and misses the concerning biochemical trend that needs urgent escalation.
options.consequence: An alarm-only note could conceal missed therapy and concerning biochemical changes.

options.text: Increase the prescribed fluid-removal goal to make up the difference.
options.feedback: Net fluid removal is not interchangeable with the delivered solute-clearance dose. Report both and ask the responsible team to reassess the prescription.
options.consequence: Increasing net fluid removal to compensate for clearance downtime could introduce haemodynamic harm.

learning_points: Assess the patient first and request the trained operator; device-specific line checks and alarm handling follow the approved procedure.
Do not use override or disable functions to clear an unresolved problem.
For persistent alarms, escalate and follow the authorized termination pathway; blood return is not automatic and must not be attempted when circuit safety is uncertain.
Report downtime, delivered solute-clearance therapy and net fluid balance separately; do not independently compensate by increasing ultrafiltration.
With regional citrate anticoagulation, escalate concerning calcium, supplementation and acid-base trends; the specialist team determines the response.
